ESV.1: “At this also my heart trembles and leaps out of its place.
ESV.2: Keep listening to the thunder of his voice and the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
ESV.3: Under the whole heaven he lets it go, and his lightning to the corners of the earth.
ESV.4: After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not restrain the lightnings  when his voice is heard.
ESV.5: God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things that we cannot comprehend.
ESV.6: For to the snow he says, ‘Fall on the earth,’ likewise to the downpour, his mighty downpour.
ESV.7: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he made may know it.
ESV.8: Then the beasts go into their lairs, and remain in their dens.
ESV.9: From its chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds.
ESV.10: By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen fast.
ESV.11: He loads the thick cloud with moisture; the clouds scatter his lightning.
ESV.12: They turn around and around by his guidance, to accomplish all that he commands them on the face of the habitable world.
ESV.13: Whether for correction or for his land or for love, he causes it to happen.
ESV.14: “Hear this, O Job; stop and consider the wondrous works of God.
ESV.15: Do you know how God lays his command upon them and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
ESV.16: Do you know the balancings  of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge,
ESV.17: you whose garments are hot when the earth is still because of the south wind?
ESV.18: Can you, like him, spread out the skies, hard as a cast metal mirror?
ESV.19: Teach us what we shall say to him; we cannot draw up our case because of darkness.
ESV.20: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Did a man ever wish that he would be swallowed up?
ESV.21: “And now no one looks on the light when it is bright in the skies, when the wind has passed and cleared them.
ESV.22: Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed with awesome majesty.
ESV.23: The Almighty — we cannot find him; he is great in power; justice and abundant righteousness he will not violate.
ESV.24: Therefore men fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own conceit.”

NKJV.1: “At this also my heart trembles, And leaps from its place.
NKJV.2: Hear attentively the thunder of His voice, And the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
NKJV.3: He sends it forth under the whole heaven, His lightning to the ends of the earth.
NKJV.4: After it a voice roars; He thunders with His majestic voice, And He does not restrain them when His voice is heard.
NKJV.5: God thunders marvelously with His voice;  He does great things which we cannot comprehend.
NKJV.6: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth’; Likewise to the gentle rain and the heavy rain of His strength.
NKJV.7: He seals the hand of every man,  That all men may know His work.
NKJV.8: The beasts go into dens, And remain in their lairs.
NKJV.9: From the chamber of the south comes the whirlwind, And cold from the scattering winds of the north.
NKJV.10: By the breath of God ice is given, And the broad waters are frozen.
NKJV.11: Also with moisture He saturates the thick clouds; He scatters His bright clouds.
NKJV.12: And they swirl about, being turned by His guidance, That they may do whatever He commands them On the face of the whole earth.
NKJV.13: He causes it to come, Whether for correction, Or for His land, Or for mercy.
NKJV.14: “Listen to this, O Job; Stand still and consider the wondrous works of God.
NKJV.15: Do you know when God dispatches them, And causes the light of His cloud to shine?
NKJV.16: Do you know how the clouds are balanced, Those wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
NKJV.17: Why are your garments hot, When He quiets the earth by the south wind?
NKJV.18: With Him, have you spread out the skies, Strong as a cast metal mirror?
NKJV.19: “Teach us what we should say to Him, For we can prepare nothing because of the darkness.
NKJV.20: Should He be told that I wish to speak? If a man were to speak, surely he would be swallowed up.
NKJV.21: Even now men cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies, When the wind has passed and cleared them.
NKJV.22: He comes from the north as golden splendor; With God is awesome majesty.
NKJV.23: As for the Almighty, we cannot find Him; He is excellent in power, In judgment and abundant justice; He does not oppress.
NKJV.24: Therefore men fear Him; He shows no partiality to any who are wise of heart.”

NLT.1:
“My heart pounds as I think of this.
It trembles within me.
NLT.2:
Listen carefully to the thunder of God’s voice
as it rolls from his mouth.
NLT.3:
It rolls across the heavens,
and his lightning flashes in every direction.
NLT.4:
Then comes the roaring of the thunder —
the tremendous voice of his majesty.
He does not restrain it when he speaks.
NLT.5:
God’s voice is glorious in the thunder.
We can’t even imagine the greatness of his power.
NLT.6:
“He directs the snow to fall on the earth
and tells the rain to pour down.
NLT.7:
Then everyone stops working
so they can watch his power.
NLT.8:
The wild animals take cover
and stay inside their dens.
NLT.9:
The stormy wind comes from its chamber,
and the driving winds bring the cold.
NLT.10:
God’s breath sends the ice,
freezing wide expanses of water.
NLT.11:
He loads the clouds with moisture,
and they flash with his lightning.
NLT.12:
The clouds churn about at his direction.
They do whatever he commands throughout the earth.
NLT.13:
He makes these things happen either to punish people
or to show his unfailing love.
NLT.14:
“Pay attention to this, Job.
Stop and consider the wonderful miracles of God!
NLT.15:
Do you know how God controls the storm
and causes the lightning to flash from his clouds?
NLT.16:
Do you understand how he moves the clouds
with wonderful perfection and skill?
NLT.17:
When you are sweltering in your clothes
and the south wind dies down and everything is still,
NLT.18:
he makes the skies reflect the heat like a bronze mirror.
Can you do that?
NLT.19:
“So teach the rest of us what to say to God.
We are too ignorant to make our own arguments.
NLT.20:
Should God be notified that I want to speak?
Can people even speak when they are confused?
NLT.21:
We cannot look at the sun,
for it shines brightly in the sky
when the wind clears away the clouds.
NLT.22:
So also, golden splendor comes from the mountain of God.
He is clothed in dazzling splendor.
NLT.23:
We cannot imagine the power of the Almighty;
but even though he is just and righteous,
he does not destroy us.
NLT.24:
No wonder people everywhere fear him.
All who are wise show him reverence. ”

WEB.1: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
WEB.2: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
WEB.3: He sends it out under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
WEB.4: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.
WEB.5: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
WEB.6: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
WEB.7: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
WEB.8: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
WEB.9: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
WEB.10: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
WEB.11: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
WEB.12: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
WEB.13: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.
WEB.14: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
WEB.15: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
WEB.16: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?
WEB.17: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?
WEB.18: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?
WEB.19: Teach us what we shall tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.
WEB.20: Will it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?
WEB.21: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.
WEB.22: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.
WEB.23: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.
WEB.24: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”

AMP.1:
"Indeed, at His thundering my heart trembles
And leaps out of its place.
AMP.2:
"Listen carefully to the thunder of His voice,
And the rumbling that goes out of His mouth!
AMP.3:
"He lets it loose under the whole heaven,
And His lightning to the ends of the earth.
AMP.4:
"After it, His voice roars;
He thunders with the voice of His majesty,
And He does not restrain His lightning [against His adversaries] when His voice is heard.
AMP.5:
"God thunders marvelously with His voice;
He does great things which we cannot comprehend.
AMP.6:
"For He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth';
And [He speaks] to the showers and to the downpour [of His mighty rains], 'Be strong.'
AMP.7:
"God seals (brings to a standstill, stops) [by severe weather] the hand of every man,
That all men [whom He has made] may know His work [that is, His sovereign power and their subjection to it].
AMP.8:
"Then the beast goes into its lair
And remains in its hiding place.
AMP.9:
"Out of its chamber comes the storm,
And cold from the north wind.
AMP.10:
"Ice is made by the breath of God,
And the expanse of the waters is frozen.
AMP.11:
"He loads the thick cloud with moisture;
He disperses the cloud of His lightning.
AMP.12:
"Its direction is turned around by His guidance,
That it may do whatever He commands it
On the face of the inhabited earth.
AMP.13:
"Whether [it be] for correction, or for His earth [generally]
Or for [His] mercy and lovingkindness, He causes it to happen.
AMP.14:
"Listen to this, Job;
Stand still and consider the wonders of God.
AMP.15:
"Do you know how God establishes and commands them,
And makes the lightning of His [storm] cloud shine?
AMP.16:
"Do you know about the layers of thick clouds [and how they are balanced and poised in the heavens],
The wonderful works of Him who is perfect in knowledge,
AMP.17:
You whose garments are hot,
When He quiets the earth [in sultry summer] with the [oppressive] south wind?
AMP.18:
"Can you, with Him, spread out the sky,
Strong as a molten mirror?
AMP.19:
"Tell us [Job] what words [of man] shall we say to such a Being;
We cannot state our case because of darkness [that is, our ignorance in the presence of the unsearchable God].
AMP.20:
"So shall it be told Him that I wish to speak?
Or should a man say that he would be swallowed up [and destroyed by God]?
AMP.21:
"Now people cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies [without being blinded],
When the wind has passed and cleared them.
AMP.22:
"Out of the north comes golden splendor [and people can hardly look on it];
Around God is awesome splendor and majesty [far too glorious for man's eyes].
AMP.23:
"The Almighty—we cannot find Him;
He is exalted in power
And He will not do violence to [nor disregard] justice and abundant righteousness.
AMP.24:
"Men therefore fear Him;
He does not regard nor respect any who are wise in heart [in their own understanding and conceit]."

“Hear this, O Job;
stop and consider the wondrous works of God.
NRSVCE.15:
Do you know how God lays his command upon them,
and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?
NRSVCE.16:
Do you know the balancings of the clouds,
the wondrous works of the one whose knowledge is perfect,
NRSVCE.17:
you whose garments are hot
when the earth is still because of the south wind?
NRSVCE.18:
Can you, like him, spread out the skies,
hard as a molten mirror?
NRSVCE.19:
Teach us what we shall say to him;
we cannot draw up our case because of darkness.
NRSVCE.20:
Should he be told that I want to speak?
Did anyone ever wish to be swallowed up?
NRSVCE.21:
Now, no one can look on the light
when it is bright in the skies,
when the wind has passed and cleared them.
NRSVCE.22:
Out of the north comes golden splendor;
around God is awesome majesty.
NRSVCE.23:
The Almighty — we cannot find him;
he is great in power and justice,
and abundant righteousness he will not violate.
NRSVCE.24:
Therefore mortals fear him;
he does not regard any who are wise in their own conceit.”

MSG.1:
"Whenever this happens, my heart stops—
I'm stunned, I can't catch my breath.
MSG.2:
Listen to it! Listen to his thunder,
the rolling, rumbling thunder of his voice.
MSG.3:
He lets loose his lightnings from horizon to horizon,
lighting up the earth from pole to pole.
MSG.4:
In their wake, the thunder echoes his voice,
powerful and majestic.
He lets out all the stops, he holds nothing back.
No one can mistake that voice—
MSG.5:
His word thundering so wondrously,
his mighty acts staggering our understanding.
MSG.6:
He orders the snow, 'Blanket the earth!'
and the rain, 'Soak the whole countryside!'
MSG.7:
No one can escape the weather—it's there.
And no one can escape from God.
MSG.8:
Wild animals take shelter,
crawling into their dens,
MSG.9:
When blizzards roar out of the north
and freezing rain crusts the land.
MSG.10:
It's God's breath that forms the ice,
it's God's breath that turns lakes and rivers solid.
MSG.11:
And yes, it's God who fills clouds with rainwater
and hurls lightning from them every which way.
MSG.12:
He puts them through their paces—first this way, then that—
commands them to do what he says all over the world.
MSG.13:
Whether for discipline or grace or extravagant love,
he makes sure they make their mark.
MSG.14:
"Job, are you listening? Have you noticed all this?
Stop in your tracks! Take in God's miracle-wonders!
MSG.15:
Do you have any idea how God does it all,
how he makes bright lightning from dark storms,
MSG.16:
How he piles up the cumulus clouds—
all these miracle-wonders of a perfect Mind?
MSG.17:
Why, you don't even know how to keep cool
on a sweltering hot day,
MSG.18:
So how could you even dream
of making a dent in that hot-tin-roof sky?
MSG.19:
"If you're so smart, give us a lesson in how to address God.
We're in the dark and can't figure it out.
MSG.20:
Do you think I'm dumb enough to challenge God?
Wouldn't that just be asking for trouble?
MSG.21:
No one in his right mind stares straight at the sun
on a clear and cloudless day.
MSG.22:
As gold comes from the northern mountains,
so a terrible beauty streams from God.
MSG.23:
"Mighty God! Far beyond our reach!
Unsurpassable in power and justice!
It's unthinkable that he'd treat anyone unfairly.
MSG.24:
So bow to him in deep reverence, one and all!
If you're wise, you'll most certainly worship him."

NET.4: After that a voice roars; he thunders with an exalted voice, and he does not hold back his lightning bolts when his voice is heard.
NET.5: God thunders with his voice in marvelous ways; he does great things beyond our understanding.
NET.6: For to the snow he says, ‘Fall to earth,’ and to the torrential rains, ‘Pour down.’
NET.7: He causes everyone to stop working, so that all people may know his work.
NET.8: The wild animals go to their lairs, and in their dens they remain.
NET.9: A tempest blows out from its chamber, icy cold from the driving winds.
NET.10: The breath of God produces ice, and the breadth of the waters freeze solid.
NET.11: He loads the clouds with moisture; he scatters his lightning through the clouds.
NET.12: The clouds go round in circles, wheeling about according to his plans, to carry out all that he commands them over the face of the whole inhabited world.
NET.13: Whether it is for punishment for his land, or whether it is for mercy, he causes it to find its mark.
